title: Question 3
stem:
An object is suspended from a vertical spring as shown in Fig. 3.1.
The object is displaced vertically and then released so that it oscillates, undergoing simple
harmonic motion.
Fig. 3.2 shows the variation with displacement x of the energy E of the oscillations.
The kinetic energy, the potential energy and the total energy of the oscillations are each
represented by one of the lines P, Q and R.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the energy that is represented by each of the lines P, Q and R.

markscheme_points.text: P: total energy Q: potential energy R: kinetic energy

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in A Level Physics theory and principles that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
parts.proper_answer: total energy Q: potential energy R: kinetic energy
walkthrough:

State the core physical principle governing this problem: A level physics theory and principles. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Apply Physics Criteria**
Explain the mechanism clearly using standard terminology:

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

Determine the period of the oscillations.

$$\text{period} = \text{....................................................}\,\mathrm{s}$$

markscheme_points.text: E = ½m2x02 or E = ½mv02 and v0 = x0

hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in simple harmonic motion connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
Hint 4: Clearly show every intermediate algebraic substitution and ensure your final value has correct physical units.
walkthrough:

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
A light card is attached to the object. The object is displaced with the same initial amplitude and then released. During each complete oscillation the total energy of the system decreases by $8.0\%$ of the total energy at the start of that oscillation.
Determine the decrease in total energy, in $\mathrm{mJ}$, of the system by the end of the first $6$ complete oscillations.

$$\text{energy lost} = \text{....................................................}\,\mathrm{mJ}$$
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in simple harmonic motion connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Simple harmonic motion. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
0.926; decrease in energy = 6.4 - (6.4 × 0.926) = 2.5 mJ
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
